record.context_brief: Replacing bounded cookies by positive-drift cookies in ballisticity

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathbb{Z}$ be the one-dimensional integer lattice and consider the standard cookie (excited) random walk. A cookie environment is a family $\omega=(\omega(z,\cdot,i))_{z\in\mathbb{Z},\,i\in\mathbb{N}}$, where for each site $z$ and each $i\ge 1$, $\omega(z,\cdot,i)$ is a probability vector on the unit vectors $\{+1,-1\}\subset\mathbb{Z}$. The $i$-th cookie at site $z$, when consumed, makes the walker take a $\pm 1$ step according to $\omega(z,\cdot,i)$. After the cookies at $z$ have been used in order, all subsequent visits to $z$ use a deterministic "placebo" cookie that yields a simple symmetric random walk step. Let $X=(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ denote the resulting walk started at $0$, and let $P$ denote the law of the random environment $\omega$.

Assumptions.
(IID) The cookie stacks $(\omega(z,\cdot,\cdot))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}}$ are i.i.d. across $z$.
(WEL) Weak ellipticity: $E\!\left[\prod_{i=1}^{\infty}\big(1\wedge\omega(0,+1,i)\big)\right]>0$ and the analogous condition for $-1$, ensuring the walk has positive probability of going arbitrarily far in either direction.
(BD) Boundedness: there exists a deterministic $M\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $P$-a.s., for every $z\in\mathbb{Z}$, the number $M(z)$ of non-placebo cookies at site $z$ satisfies $M(z)\le M$.
(POS$_1$) Positivity: $P$-a.s., for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$, the drift of the $i$-th cookie at $0$ in the $+1$ direction is nonnegative, i.e., $\omega(0,+1,i)-\omega(0,-1,i)\ge 0$.

Define the average total drift
$$\delta := E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\big(\omega(0,+1,i)-\omega(0,-1,i)\big)\right]\in[-\infty,\infty].$$

Known result. Under (IID), (BD), and (WEL), the limiting velocity $v=\lim_{n\to\infty} X_n/n$ exists $P$-a.s. and satisfies $v<0$ if $\delta<-2$, $v=0$ if $\delta\in[-2,2]$, and $v>0$ if $\delta>2$.

Question. Can the boundedness assumption (BD) in the above speed dichotomy be replaced by the weaker condition (POS$_1$)? That is, assuming (IID), (WEL), and (POS$_1$) (without any deterministic upper bound on the number of non-placebo cookies per site), does the same trichotomy for the sign of the limiting velocity in terms of $\delta$ continue to hold?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has extended the one-dimensional speed/ballisticity theorem beyond the bounded-cookies assumption (BD) toward (POS_1)-type settings. In particular, O. Chakhtoun's 2019 CUNY PhD thesis "One-Dimensional Excited Random Walk with Unboundedly Many Excitations Per Site" provides criteria for recurrence/transience and ballisticity versus zero speed under tail-decay assumptions on the number of excitations per site, extending the bounded-cookie framework. Related work (e.g., long-range/one-cookie random walks and Markovian cookie stacks) addresses portions of the question. A fully general resolution under only (IID), (WEL), and (POS_1) without additional integrability or tail conditions does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: One-Dimensional Excited Random Walk with Unboundedly Many Excitations Per Site (Chakhtoun, PhD thesis, CUNY, 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a discrete time excited random walk on Z with tail decay estimates on the number of excitations per site, giving criteria for recurrence versus transience, ballisticity versus zero linear speed, and classifying limit laws.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a partial extension of the speed/ballisticity theorem beyond the bounded-cookies assumption, addressing the spirit of replacing (BD) by a positivity/tail-decay condition.

status_evidence.title: Long range one-cookie random walk with positive speed (Stochastic Processes and their Applications, 2021; arXiv:2011.00493)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs and analyzes one-cookie random walks with non-nearest-neighbor steps that exhibit positive linear speed, beyond the standard bounded-cookies framework.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress on ballisticity for cookie walks outside the (BD) setting, indicating partial advances on the question.

status_evidence.title: Excited random walks with Markovian cookie stacks (arXiv:1504.06280)
status_evidence.snippet: Generalizes the i.i.d. bounded-cookie model to Markovian (and hence possibly unboundedly many) cookie stacks, obtaining recurrence/transience and ballisticity criteria.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates that the bounded-cookies hypothesis can be relaxed in important cases, supporting partial progress on the open problem.
